prompt: Scan source text and report which public members have no doc comment above them. Complete UndocumentedMethodCounter and run the tests.
explanation: Source text is just lines, so a documentation audit becomes a scan with a backwards look: find the declaration, skip blank lines above it, and confirm the comment that ends there was opened with the doc-comment marker. Splitting the check into small private helpers -- one to name the member, one to decide whether it is documented -- keeps the main loop honest. Watch the order of the two startsWith tests when walking up: "/**" must be checked before "/*", because every doc comment opener also starts with a plain block comment opener.
hints: Split the source with source.split("\n", -1) and use the index of each member line so you can walk backwards from it.
To name the member, cut the text before the '(' and take the last word of it.
Walking up from the closing "*/", test startsWith("/**") before startsWith("/*") -- otherwise every doc comment looks like a plain block comment.
